scope: Fresh mailbox provisioning, authenticated list access and short-term reuse only. No message sent or message body read; no delivery, sending, registration acceptance or long-term retention claim.
configuration: OpenCode 1.18.35 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / high. Same v2 task, fresh isolated identities/containers, execution 25 model requests / 300 seconds, grading 40 / 300, 32000 output tokens per request. Two service streams, each 2 GiB / 1 CPU / pids256. Same base image and preconfigured TUNA pip index, empty initial package caches. No supplied service or human mailbox credentials.
preparation_disclosure: Task v2 explicitly permits the minimum anonymous upstream identity needed for one mailbox. Old v1 and its model/harness remain unchanged.
No peer answer packet for these access runs. Each independent grader checks its own captured creation/read evidence plus controller receipts; no live credentials.
Controller GET readback is extra verification time/requests outside executor allowance. Source hashes retain private exact identities and responses.

A private container-name mapping mistake failed locally before SSH/worker start. Zero remote model/API calls verified; unused owned containers removed and correct fresh containers prepared before actual dispatch. No task input or prior service result was changed.
actual_result: A new provider-domain mailbox was created inside execution, authenticated list returned empty, password/token and identity were saved privately. Independent GET /me and GET /messages?page=1 returned HTTP200 with matching identity and empty JSON list using the saved token.
interpretation_limit: Controller requested application/json and received [], while executor had JSON-LD/Hydra metadata. The initial controller parser expected only Hydra; corrected before grading on the same immutable response, without another HTTP call. Different content negotiation is not service failure.
service_attribution: Mail.tm https://mail.tm/ ; official API documentation https://docs.mail.tm/ . Free API applies to this low-volume anonymous mailbox. Mailbox and message retention differ; no permanent account-recovery claim.
cleanup: Controller rechecked the exact newly created account with GET /me, then DELETE /accounts/{id} returned204. Subsequent old-token GET /me returned401. This confirms deletion acceptance and revoked access, not a separate public absence query. No other account touched.
